original_card.question: Does one quantified step of the proposed #4100 all-size construction hold at its actual caller?
methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read PROOF.md and AUDIT.md in #4100. Select one distinct obligation: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lifting, precision/conditioning, or complete fixed-tape cost. This is an author-submitted proof, not an accepted unconditional theorem.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live handoffs; name one proposition, its caller, quantified domain and dependency closure. Independently prove the implication or exhibit a precise gap/counterexample. Prioritize CRT.md total repair or COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift only if unclaimed. Stop at the chosen obligation; do not substitute finite samples or root arithmetic for an all-size proof, or launch the complete package by default.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: One CRT repair, native lift, precision/conditioning or tape-cost proposition, with its exact caller.
scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.
Treating archive intake, an author PASS receipt or a finite composed fixture as discharge of the universal hypotheses.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: proposed unconditional construction and finite checks, without independent acceptance.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent proof audit of one caller-bound all-size implication; all other premises remain explicit.

actual_scope: Determine the exact paid_children count and total child width of the retained fallback program for every rank-r projector header, prove that the head-bank elimination makes exactly r opposite-bank swaps, and give the sharp maximum with an explicit rank-one witness.
scope_change_reason: PR4215 open question 2 and PR4228's package open question ask for the fallback child count after accounting for swap orientations. FALLBACK.md's 49911 bound charges three children per swap. This is a sharp count for that one tape-cost term, not an audit of the rest of PR4100.
bottleneck_link: FALLBACK.md's child count enters the auxiliary BIT recurrence's fallback toll. A sharp count tightens that term; it cannot move kappa by itself.
stop_rule: Stop after the written count, the m<=64 witness family, small complete idempotent censuses and controls; no physical fallback execution or recurrence retuning.
evidence: README.md proves the rank law and closed forms. verify.py checks them through the unchanged prepare/paid_children path on a rank-one witness for every 2<=m<=64, an integer replay valid for every odd modulus, complete idempotent censuses (332 idempotents) and 24 seeded m=64 headers.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Is the same-bank elimination swap count at most 2(m-r) for every rank-r header?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would give the exact rank-dependent maximum 8m^2+8m-6-5r; the proved ceiling 2m-1-r is attained only at r=1 in the censuses.
open_questions.first_step: Track which original rows occupy tail positions at the start of the tail phase and bound swaps there by m-r.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing; it is a linear-algebra question.

open_questions.question: Which headers actually reach the fallback in the auxiliary BIT recurrence, and with what rank distribution?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The sharp maximum is attained only by rank-one headers; a caller that sends only higher ranks pays less.
open_questions.first_step: Bind the recurrence's fallback branch in BIT.md to its header ranks.
